conviction_note: A print at or a little above the 6-8% guide is likely, since Q2 came in at 17% against a 14-16% guide. But the last three prints each fell about 7% on decelerating guides. The stock is up 11.6% over 20 days, and Cash App issuance is going to zero by year end with a larger 2027 drag already flagged. So the lean is slightly negative (p_up 46) on a large absolute move (10%, between the 8.9% median reaction and the indicative 12.4% implied move). The findings sum to -0.5, and the scaled number is -0.8; the two agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Company guide for Q3 2026: net revenue growth 6-8% (about $173.1M-$176.4M, midpoint $174.7M), gross profit growth 5-7%, adjusted EBITDA growth 20-25% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001522540/000152254026000061/mqearningsrelease-q2x2026.htm, 2026-08-04). Street consensus is disputed: Benzinga $175.1M (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/MQ/earnings-forecasts) against Earnings Whispers $180.2M (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MQ), and the EW figure looks like a pre-guide number. EPS consensus about $0.05 (Benzinga/Chartmill). Sized against the company guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,530,874 shares, 5.04% of float, 4.6 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15, down 3.3% from 4,684,723 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MQ/short-interest/, FINRA publication 2026-10-26). Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew null (not computable). Put/call open-interest ratio 0.02 on total open interest of only 1,869. The ATM spread is 45% of mid, so the 12.37% event-implied move is indicative only. Run-up +11.6% over 20 days and +2.4% over 5 days; 9.1% below the 52-week high. The option market makes no usable directional statement.

findings.finding: Marqeta has beaten its own quarterly revenue guide: Q2 2026 net revenue grew 17% ($176.0M) against a 14-16% guide, and adjusted EBITDA grew 31%. The Q3 guide is 6-8% (about $173.1-176.4M), so a repeat beat of 1-3 points puts Q3 at roughly 8-10%, or $176-180M. That is about +1.5% against the guide midpoint and at or slightly above the $175.1M Benzinga consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat its revenue guide and the stock fell 7.13%. Q1 2026 (19% growth) fell 7.7% and Q4 2025 fell 7.21%. Earlier beats in 2025 rose 8.9-21%. The last three beats were sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus already sits at or above the guide midpoint, and a habitual beater's beat is expected. The Q3 figure itself is unseen. If the market expected a large beat, consensus would sit near $180M on every source, not split between $175M and $180M.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001522540/000152254026000036/mqearningsrelease-q1x2026.htm) shows 19% Q1 growth. The FY revenue guide was narrowed from 12-14% to 12-13% in August, which partly argues against a large beat.

findings.finding: The forward line is the Cash App issuance shift. Management said new Cash App issuance began declining in mid-June and expects little to no new issuance by year end. The Cash App drag in 2027 will be 'a little bit more' than the about 2 points expected for 2026. Q4 should show 'similar trends' to Q3. The FY 12-13% guide implies Q4 net revenue growth of only about 6.6-10.2%. Block was 41% of Q2 net revenue, and Q4 guidance plus any 2027 color is due on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each of the last three prints carried a decelerating forward guide and fell 7.1-7.7% (2026-08-04, 2026-05-05, 2026-02-24). Q2's guide to 6-8% Q3 growth came with -7.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: The deceleration itself is public. Not priced is the size of the 2027 step-down, which management declined to quantify ('details in early 2027'). Whether Q4 is guided to the low end of the implied 6.6-10.2% is also open. The 11.6% 20-day run-up toward the 52-week high is not what a market bracing for another step-down would show.
findings.independence: eMarketer on the same call (https://www.emarketer.com/content/marqeta-will-issue--little-no--new-cash-app-cards-by-year-end). Same document, not independent. Block's own Q2 letter shows Cash App Commerce Enablement volume +17%, driven by Cash App Card (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001512673/000119312526335117/d91486dex991.htm). That supports the existing Block card base on Marqeta, which offsets part of this.

findings.finding: Klarna, a Marqeta customer since 2018 for US virtual cards and the Klarna Card, reported 6.5M Klarna Card active users at Q2 2026, up from 1.3M a year earlier. It also cut FY GMV guidance to $149-151B and guided Q3 GMV to $35-36B, with late-Q2 softness continuing into Q3. Marqeta's lending/BNPL TPV slowed from about 60% to over 40% in Q2, and it guided over 30% for H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No line-specific history. BNPL is 1-2 points of Marqeta's guided Q3 deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: Klarna spoke two weeks after Marqeta's guide. Its card scaling (5x actives) is the part Marqeta processes and is not reflected in Marqeta's 30%+ H2 BNPL guide. Its GMV softness points the other way. It is a proxy with mixed sign, hence small.
findings.independence: Marqeta powers the Klarna Card in the US and in 15 European markets (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251103343270/en/Marqeta-Powers-Expansion-of-Klarna-Debit-Card-Across-Europe). Marqeta also disclosed that one BNPL customer is load-balancing virtual-card volume to other providers, which cuts against this.

findings.finding: DoorDash's Q3 2026 total orders grew 28% Y/Y to 993M and Marketplace GOV 36% to $33.9B, including Deliveroo. On-demand delivery is a Marqeta vertical that grew double digits in Q2 but below the company rate, with mix shifting to less favorable economics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. Management flagged a lower take rate in this vertical in Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer printed after Marqeta last spoke. This is a sector proxy: no source here confirms which delivery platforms run on Marqeta, and the Deliveroo orders are largely non-US. Small.
findings.independence: Marqeta's own Q2 call commentary on on-demand delivery (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-marqeta-inc-stock/) says the take rate is falling, which partly offsets the volume.

findings.finding: Visa's calendar Q3 2026 payments volume grew 9% Y/Y in constant dollars, with cross-border +14%. Card spending was steady through the quarter Marqeta reports, consistent with Marqeta's 'not seeing a notable shift in spend or consumer behavior'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marqeta TPV has grown 32-33% against network volume near 9-10%, so macro explains little of its print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It only rules out a macro-driven TPV miss. Macro proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: Block (Marqeta's 41% customer) reports Q3 2026 the same evening after the close, with its call at 5:00 pm ET. Its Cash App Card and Commerce Enablement commentary lands inside the window, alongside Marqeta's own call at 4:30 pm ET.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history for coincident Block prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknowable before the release. Filed because it widens the reaction (abs_move) and a judge may weigh it. It carries no sign.
findings.independence: The sweep row independently flags Block's same-evening print.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock is up 11.6% over 20 days and about 15% since mid-September (a director's 10b5-1 sale was at about $16.09 on 2026-09-16, now $18.47), 9% below its 52-week high. Short interest is a modest 5.04% of float with 4.6 days to cover, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The run-up raises the bar on a name whose last three beats were sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints each fell about 7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price itself. I found no news explaining the October rise, so the rally reads as positioning into an expected beat rather than repricing on a disclosed fact.

findings.finding: The board authorized a new $150M buyback on 2026-08-03 after exhausting the December 2025 program; $93.9M was repurchased in H1 2026. Q3 repurchase volume and share-count reduction will be disclosed in this print, on a market cap of about $4.2B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior authorization did not prevent the -7% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. The pace of Q3 use is not, and an aggressive pace would support per-share figures.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as the Q2 release. Not independent.

findings.finding: Finance and governance turnover since the last print: the Chief Accounting Officer resigned effective 2026-08-21 with no successor named (the CFO takes over as principal accounting officer; the filing states 'not due to any disagreement'); a director resigned 2026-08-03; a new Chief Product Officer started 2026-08-31.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, quiet 8-Ks. Probably noise, and the filing explicitly disclaims any accounting disagreement.

outside_window.finding: DoorDash agreed on 2026-10-29 to acquire Instacart (Maplebear) for about $17B, closing end-2027 or H1 2028. Any consolidation of on-demand card programs for Marqeta would come long after this window, and I found no source tying either platform to Marqeta.
The 2027 Cash App run-rate drag ('a little bit more' than 2 points) will be quantified in early 2027, per management. Any partial color on this call is in the guidance finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Sits above the company's own guide published the same day; Benzinga's $175.1M matches the guide. Treated as a stale pre-guide figure, and the bar is the company guide.

baseline_tension: No usable skew. The 11.6% run-up and the last three -7% reactions to beats lean against a positive read of a likely guide beat, so the findings and p_up lean slightly negative. Short interest (5%) is too small to mount a squeeze against that lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last three beats): reported-quarter guide-beat finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): Q4 'similar trends' was already guided, so the guidance finding moved toward 0, from -1.0 to -0.8. The bar is sourced to the company guide; the disputed EW consensus goes to rejected_candidates.
Lesson 5 (proxies stay filed and small): Klarna, DoorDash and Visa kept at +0.2/+0.2/+0.1 as proxies; no change.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked at 5.04% of float, not crowded, so the negative positioning finding stands at -0.5. abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
